lines: Nine people got on the last train.
It left Harlow station at eleven fifty-two, on a cold night in March.
The missing man left a coat, a cold coffee, and a ticket he never used.
The train did not stop on the way.
But inside the tunnel it slowed down, at a red signal, for forty seconds.
When it arrived, a bank courier opened his case.
The signal had been switched by hand, from the desk of the night guard.
He told the police he saw nothing.
But the signal log keeps every switch, to the second.
And the ninth passenger was his brother.
